title: Provider onboards a new managed client end-to-end in "invite owner" mode
description: Exercises the full /mssp/clients/new wizard (clients/new/page.jsx) against POST /mssp/clients with ownerMode="invite".
preconditions: Logged in as an MSSP_OWNER on an active MSSP provider
Provider has at least one licensed framework and one active project plan
steps: Navigate to /mssp/clients/new
Fill in organization name/domain, owner first/last name/email, and one project with a plan and a licensed framework
Click "Create client & invite owner"
Observe the completion screen, then open the new client from /mssp/clients
expectedResult: A new client organization (kind=mssp_client) and MsspClientRelationship (status=active, accessModel=client_owner) are created; the owner receives an email invitation (TenantInvitation type=mssp_client_user) and cannot yet log in until it is accepted; the client appears in /mssp/clients with its project(s) pending billing setup as described on the completion screen.

title: Provider onboards a managed client in "add owner" mode and the one-time temporary password is shown exactly once
description: Covers clients/new/page.jsx's completion screen for ownerMode='add' (lines 143-167): the Code/copy UI, and the distinct warning shown if the temporary password is unavailable because the create call was a replay.
steps: Complete the new-client form and submit via "Create client & add owner"
On the completion screen, copy the displayed temporary password using the copy button
Refresh the page (or otherwise re-render the completion state) and confirm the password is not re-displayed anywhere in the UI or re-fetchable from the API
expectedResult: The temporary password is shown once, copies correctly to the clipboard (button flips to a checkmark), and is not recoverable afterward through any client-panel screen or API response — matching MSSP-SEC-006.

title: Provider onboards a client as "MSSP-managed" — no client-side login is created and the access model badge reflects it
description: Covers ownerMode='provider_managed', where the same auditor/contact email can safely be reused across multiple client onboardings because no client User record is created. Grounded in clients/new/page.jsx completion text and clients/[clientOrgId]/page.jsx's accessModel badge (purple 'MSSP managed' vs blue 'Client owner').
steps: Onboard a client using "Create as MSSP-managed", entering the same contact email already used as the owner contact on a previous, different client
Open the new client's detail page at /mssp/clients/:clientOrgId
expectedResult: Onboarding succeeds without a duplicate-email conflict; the client detail page shows the "MSSP managed" badge; the Users & invitations tab (if visible) shows no client-side user created for that contact; the provider retains full management access via its own MSSP session.

title: A failure partway through client onboarding fully rolls back — no orphaned organization, relationship, or Keycloak org is left behind
description: mssp.controller.js createClient catch block (lines 224-230): on any error after the organization is created, it deletes the MsspClientRelationship, calls provisioning.cleanupOrganization(org) (which deletes ProjectMembers/Projects/TenantInvitations/Users/subscriptions/the Organization/the Keycloak org), and marks the ProvisioningOperation "failed".
preconditions: Provider licensed catalog does NOT include a framework code the tester will deliberately request for the second project, forcing resolveLicensedFrameworks to throw mid-flow
steps: Submit POST /mssp/clients with two projects, where the second project requests an unlicensed framework code
After the call fails, search the admin panel's direct-customer/organization list and Keycloak for the attempted organization domain
Retry the exact same request (same Idempotency-Key) with corrected, fully-licensed frameworks
expectedResult: The initial call returns an error and leaves no trace: no Organization, no MsspClientRelationship, no Keycloak organization for that domain, and the ProvisioningOperation ends in status "failed". The retry with the same idempotency key and corrected payload succeeds (since the original attempt did not complete) and creates the client cleanly.

title: Once NEXT_PUBLIC_MSSP_PORTAL_URL is configured, an authenticated MSSP user is redirected OUT of every /mssp/* client-panel page, including ones they navigate to directly
description: middleware.js:96-101: when isMssp is true AND pathname starts with '/mssp' AND NEXT_PUBLIC_MSSP_PORTAL_URL is set and does not start with 'RUNTIME_', the client-panel unconditionally redirects to the external Partner Portal instead of rendering its own (mssp) route group — the embedded /mssp/dashboard fallback (line 32) only applies when that env var is unset. This is a distinct angle from RBAC-E2E-005, which assumes the embedded-fallback configuration.
preconditions: NEXT_PUBLIC_MSSP_PORTAL_URL is set to a real Partner Portal origin (not prefixed RUNTIME_)
Logged in via SSO as an mssp_provider user in the client-panel session
steps: Manually navigate the browser to https://<client-panel host>/mssp/dashboard
Manually navigate to https://<client-panel host>/mssp/clients/new
expectedResult: Both navigations redirect to <configured MSSP portal>/auth/login?source=client-portal — the client-panel's own (mssp) route group is never rendered once this environment variable is configured, so its 11 page files become unreachable dead routes in that deployment.

title: A non-MSSP (customer) session opening the Partner Portal is bounced to a distinct "NotMsspAccount" error, not the client-panel dashboard
description: vibrantix-partner-portal/src/middleware.js:22-24,33-39 is a separate implementation from vibrantix-client-panel's middleware.js: a non-MSSP authenticated token hitting '/' or '/auth/login' or any private path is redirected to /auth/error?error=NotMsspAccount, never to a customer dashboard (the Partner Portal has no customer-facing pages to fall back to).
preconditions: A direct_customer or mssp_client user has a valid NextAuth session token with portalMode !== "mssp"
steps: Reuse that session (or its cookie) against the Partner Portal origin's "/" path
Navigate to the Partner Portal's /dashboard directly
expectedResult: Both attempts redirect to /auth/error?error=NotMsspAccount. No Partner Portal private page (dashboard, clients, team, etc.) ever renders for a non-MSSP token.

title: Provider team member invitation lifecycle: invite, resend cooldown, and revoke deprovisions access
steps: From /mssp/team, invite a new MSSP_OPERATOR team member (invite mode)
Open /mssp/invitations, confirm the new invite shows status "pending"
Immediately click Resend a second time within 60 seconds
Wait out the cooldown, resend again successfully, then Revoke the invitation
expectedResult: The invite appears pending with the correct role and expiry; the immediate second resend is rejected with a "wait one minute" conflict; the later resend succeeds and refreshes the expiry; revoke sets status to "revoked", disables the pending Keycloak user, and removes any reserved project access.

title: Platform admin onboards a new MSSP provider, licenses two frameworks, and the provider can only onboard clients within that catalog
description: End-to-end across vibrantix-admin-panel (/tenant-management/mssps/new, provider detail page's "Licensed framework pool") and vibrantix-client-panel's /mssp/clients/new framework picker, tying admin.controller.js onboardMssp/replaceFrameworkCatalog to mssp.controller.js listFrameworkCatalog/resolveLicensedFrameworks.
preconditions: Platform admin session with admin:mssp scope
steps: From /tenant-management/mssps/new, onboard a new MSSP with no owner yet (provision-only) and no frameworks
Open the provider detail page and license exactly ISO 27001 and SOC 2 via "Licensed framework pool" → Save pool
From that same detail page, invite the MSSP owner
As the newly invited owner, log into the client-panel and open /mssp/clients/new
expectedResult: The provider's /mssp/clients/new framework checklist offers exactly ISO 27001 and SOC 2 (from GET /mssp/frameworks) and no others; attempting to submit a project with any other framework is impossible from the UI and is independently rejected server-side per MSSP-SEC-005.

title: Platform admin detaches a single managed client to direct ownership and the preview counts match the outcome
description: admin-panel's mssps/[providerId]/page.jsx detachClient() calls detachPreview() to build its confirmation prompt, then detachClient(). Backend: admin.controller.js previewDetach/detachClient, OwnershipTransfer, MsspAuditEvent 'mssp.client.detached'.
preconditions: MSSP provider with at least one active managed client that has 1+ projects and 1+ users
steps: Open the provider detail page and note the client's row (status, project count)
Click Detach, read the confirmation dialog's reported project/user/subscription counts, and provide a reason
Confirm the detach, then reload the provider detail page and the platform admin's direct-customer list
expectedResult: The confirmation counts equal the client's actual project/user/subscription totals; after confirming, the client no longer appears among the provider's active managed clients, its Organization.kind is now direct_customer with all data preserved, and it appears in the direct-customers list; an MsspAuditEvent with action "mssp.client.detached" and the given reason is recorded.

title: Platform admin de-owns an entire MSSP provider — every managed client converts to a direct customer in one action
description: admin.controller.js detachAllClients: bulk-updates every non-detached MsspClientRelationship to 'detached', flips every affected Organization.kind to direct_customer, and sets the MsspProvider itself to status='deowned' in one pass, recording a single 'mssp.deowned' audit event with detachedClientCount.
preconditions: MSSP provider with 3+ active managed clients
steps: From the provider detail page, click "De-own MSSP" and provide a reason
After confirmation, attempt to load the provider's own /mssp/dashboard as its owner user
Check each formerly-managed client individually in the direct-customers list
expectedResult: All previously-managed clients now show kind=direct_customer with their data intact; the provider's MsspProvider.status is "deowned"; the former provider owner can no longer use /mssp/dashboard (denied per MSSP-SEC-003, since status is no longer "active"); one audit event records the total detached count.
